sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203].
Operating income grew faster at 12.3% and net income at 14.7%, lifting operating margin from 3.2% to 3.9% [F204][F205][F23][F32].
FY2021 was the first inflection, with revenue up 17.5% on a 16% comparable sales increase and strong non-foods and e-commerce [D189][P56].
FY2022 repeated the step, revenue up 15.8%, as comparable sales rose 14% with inflation and gasoline, business centers and travel leading [D238][P42].
The US segment supplied 72.5% of FY2026 revenue and 7.2pp of growth, with Other International adding 1.6pp [D670][D672][D679].
FY2026 net sales rose $27.3 billion, 10%, on comparable sales up 8% from 5% higher average ticket and 3% more shopping frequency [P14].
Food and Sundries remained the largest product line at 38.5% of revenue but contributed only 2.6pp, while warehouse ancillary added 3.7pp [D558][D560][D601].
Membership fees grew 11.0% to $5.9 billion on new sign-ups, fee increases and Executive upgrades [D664][S78][P13].
Operating income grew 12.5% against 10.1% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 4.7% [D435][D434][D457].
FY2026 operating margin of 3.9% is the window high, above the 3.4% median and the 3.1% low [F32][D691][D692][D690].
The latest year's 0.1pp gain came from SG&A, up 8.9% against 10.1% revenue growth, while cost of revenue was neutral [D447][D450][D434][D459][D460].
SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of sales, though currency moves added $126 million to the expense [P9].
Gross margin slipped three basis points, with mix into faster-growing ancillary businesses offset by core merchandise gains and tariff refunds [P12].
Net margin of 3.0% trails operating margin by 0.8pp, with the 24.7% tax rate the main wedge [F52][F32][D732][D420].
Operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income, near the 1.75x window median [F82][F42][D421][D722].
The 18.6% operating cash flow increase came from higher operating income and reduced net inventory investment on faster turns and better supplier terms [D439][P6].
Free cash flow of $9.4 billion was a 3.1% margin, above the 2.8% median, after capex of $6.4 billion, 2.1% of revenue [F102][D418][D698][F92][D417].
Capex ran at 2.41x D&A, the highest ratio in the window, as the warehouse build accelerated [D423].
Net cash reached $15.1 billion, 5.0% of revenue, up from $9.5 billion, ranking at the 100th percentile of four retail peers [D427][D428][D378][D733].
Total debt was $6.2 billion, with $2.2 billion current, against $21.3 billion of cash and investments [D426][X160][D425].
Buybacks and dividends of $3.3 billion absorbed 35.2% of free cash flow, and the share count was flat at 444.4 million [D429][D430][X100].
Financing outflow of $3.4 billion covered dividends, repurchases and debt repayment, partly offset by $496 million of new debt [F122][P4][X130].
Operating margin sits at the 17th percentile of six retail peers against a 5.0% median, so the model runs on volume, not margin [D709][D710].
Free cash flow margin sits at the 50th percentile of six retail peers against a 4.2% peer median [D713][D714].
Capex has grown 17.0% while revenue grew 10.1%, pushing capex to 2.41x D&A and compressing free cash flow conversion [D441][D434][D423].
Receivables grew 23.6%, faster than revenue, lifting days sales outstanding to 5 days from 4 [D455][D431].
If operating margin holds at or above the FY2026 high of 3.9%, the leverage story continues; a slip toward the 3.4% median would reverse it [F32][D691][D692].
Watch capex against the FY2026 level of $6.4 billion; further growth would keep free cash flow margin below the 3.6% window high [F92][D697].
Membership fee growth above the FY2026 11.0% would confirm the fee engine; a fall toward the FY2024 5.4% would flag renewal pressure [D664][D658].
